papers.title: A source-based decomposition of thermal noise for mechanical system design
papers.abstract: Thermal noise limits the sensitivity of precision mechanical instruments. We present a thermal- noise formulation for lumped-element mechanical systems that writes the total displacement thermal noise at the readout as the sum of contributions from all dissipative elements. For each contribution, we separate the thermal force generated by the element from its transfer to the readout. This decomposition provides simple design rules for comparing contributions from elements in series and in parallel and identifying the dominant noise source. It applies to frequency-dependent dissipation and to elements at different steady temperatures under local thermal equilibrium. We use it to identify the frequency regimes in which parallel and series dissipation dilution reduce displacement thermal noise. We then use examples of a pendulum on a lossy support, a rotational flexure, and rigidly mounted lunar optics to show how support noise can dominate even when the support has little effect on the system dynamics. Finally, a feedback-controlled suspension illustrates how sensing and actuation noise can be included in the same displacement-noise budget.

papers.title: A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies
papers.abstract: We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $\Lambda_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.

papers.title: Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity
papers.abstract: In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.

papers.title: A Wideband Technosignature Search of 210,191 Nearby Main-sequence Stars with the VLA Sky Survey
papers.abstract: Searches for radio technosignatures have concentrated on narrowband signals. We present a complementary search for excess broadband 2-4 GHz emission from 210,191 Gaia DR3 main-sequence stars within 100 pc in all epochs of the VLA Sky Survey (VLASS; 2017-2026). Cross-matching with the Epoch-1 catalog yields 51 high-reliability positional associations (versus 1.5 expected by chance). All but one are known natural emitters that, where measurable, move with their stars; the remaining source, near LSPM J1943+5337, is not at the star. Because stellar flares can mimic transmitters in continuum flux, a detection counts as a possible transmitter at any luminosity only at the 32,985 apparently single AFGK stars outside known radio-emitter classes, and at M dwarfs and AFGK multiples only above $10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Forced photometry of 208,232 stars in all epochs finds 1 steady-test detection and 3 stars detected in at least one epoch among the eligible stars, against 1.3 and 1.9 expected by chance. The median per-star limit on steady emission is $L_\nu<4.0\times10^{8}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Without background subtraction, fewer than $1.5\times10^{-4}$ of eligible AFGK stars host a steady transmitter above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$, and fewer than $2.3\times10^{-5}$ of all stars outside the known-emitter classes host one above $\sim1.1\times10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$; counting every M-dwarf detection as a possible transmitter, fewer than $5.5\times10^{-4}$ of M dwarfs host one above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Stacks detect population-averaged emission from M dwarfs, concentrated in those with activity evidence. Continuum surveys thus constrain broadband, modulated, or rapidly drifting signals that narrowband pipelines do not search for.

papers.title: Entanglement island and Page curve for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the information paradox for one-sided asymptotically flat rotating Kerr black holes formed through gravitational collapse using the island prescription. Near the horizon, the dynamics of a scalar field can be described by an effective two-dimensional theory, which provides the framework for our analysis. We study how rotation affects the location of the island boundary $\partial I$, the Page time, and the scrambling time, treating non-extremal and extremal Kerr black holes separately. For non-extremal black holes, the emergence of an island prevents the unbounded growth of Hawking radiation entropy at late times and restores the unitary Page curve. We further find that the island boundary depends on the location of the cutoff surface, in contrast to the behaviour found for eternal Kerr black holes. In the extremal case, the late-time entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation approaches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the extremal black hole. Our results demonstrate the important role of black hole geometry in determining the behaviour of entanglement entropy and suggest that the island prescription provides a semiclassical resolution of the information paradox for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes.

papers.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12\pi/\Lambda$, for de Sitter, or at most $4\pi/\Lambda$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $\pi_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

papers.title: Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider
papers.abstract: We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.

papers.title: Constraining the Binary Fraction and Mass-Ratio Distribution of FGK Dwarfs with Gaia XP Spectra: Metallicity, $α$-Element, and Age Dependencies
papers.abstract: We present a study of the binary fraction and mass-ratio distribution for near 200,000 FGK dwarf stars within 1 kpc, utilizing the Stellar Locus Outlier (SLOT) method applied to synthetic Gaia XP photometry and stellar parameters from LAMOST DR9. Our results shed light on how chemical composition and dynamical processes shape the binary properties of solar-type stars.

papers.title: A Gauge Pathway to an Ultralight Axion through a Hidden Portal
papers.abstract: We study a gauge realization of an ultralight axion with a hidden $SU(2)$ interaction, an Abelian vector portal, a charged Higgs and a Stückelberg field. The vector absorbs one scalar combination and leaves a physical phase. Its normalization is fixed by the Higgs and Stückelberg scales, while hidden confinement generates its mass. Keeping this phase ultralight requires an additional symmetry: the displayed gauge charges alone allow large phase-dependent scalar interactions. We quantify the suppression required of these interactions. Pure-$SU(2)$ lattice results relate the susceptibility to physical confinement scales; one- and two-loop running illustrate the dependence on the chosen high-energy coupling. We derive the coherent radiation-era density and exhibit an initial angle giving the reference dark-matter abundance for $F_\chi\simeq10^{17}\,\GeV$ and zero-temperature mass $m_{\chi,0}=3\times10^{-20}\,\eV$. We follow the confined population through number-changing and number-conserving limits and bound its energy contribution. An illustrative inflaton background satisfies the stated vacuum and isocurvature tests, conditional on control of a large portal correction to its potential. Its cold hidden history requires a hidden-to-visible reheating fraction near $5\times10^{-12}$, whose microscopic origin remains an input. A second, gauge-anomaly-free model gives the same physical phase scale using two charged Higgs singlets. These constructions specify conditional cosmological examples and the additional protection and reheating mechanisms needed to complete them.

papers.title: The Alma catalog of OB stars. IV. A massive star census of the Magellanic Clouds System
papers.abstract: Context. The Magellanic Clouds System (MCS), comprising the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) and the Magellanic Bridge (MB), offers a nearby laboratory for studying massive stars. Existing catalogs are limited by extinction, crowding, and incomplete cross-validation with the literature. Aims. We identify candidate stars with initial masses of roughly 8 solar masses or more, including O- and early-B-type stars, supergiants, luminous blue variables, and Wolf-Rayet stars. We aim to improve completeness in reddened and crowded regions and recover sources missed by large surveys. Methods. We combine Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with SIMBAD, HST, and complementary optical and infrared surveys. We select candidates using color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, extinction tracks, Gaia astrometry and variability, and spectral classifications. We check for duplicates and multiple systems, include literature and HST-resolved sources without reliable Gaia counterparts, especially in 30 Dor, and derive synthetic Gaia photometry where Gaia measurements are incomplete. Results. ALS IV contains 51 954 massive star candidates: 36 506 in the LMC, 15 264 in the SMC, and 184 in the MB. It provides homogeneous identifiers and coordinates, multiwavelength photometry, astrometry, variability diagnostics, and spectral classifications where available. Complementary photometry and HST observations recover reddened and crowded sources missed by Gaia-based selections. The sample traces the main massive-star populations and prominent star-forming regions across the MCS. Conclusions. ALS IV provides the most comprehensive census of massive star candidates in the MCS and serves as a reference for massive-star studies and future surveys and Gaia releases.

papers.title: MINDS: The mid-infrared spectrum of the disk, jets, and winds of DG Tau
papers.abstract: DG Tau is one of the best-studied young stellar objects in transition from a Class I protostar to a T Tauri star. It is no longer embedded in a dense molecular cloud, but still reveals features that are commonly seen in protostars at earlier evolutionary stages. DG Tau hosts a protoplanetary disk and two energetic jets that can be studied down to the immediate environment of the star and disk at optical, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths. We use the Medium Resolution Spectrometer of MIRI on the James Webb Space Telescope. DG Tau's mid-infrared spectrum consists of a very bright continuum with various silicate features, and lines of CO, H$_2$O, OH, H I, H$_2$, Ne$^{+}$, Ne$^{2+}$, Ar$^{+}$, Fe$^{+}$, and Ni$^{+}$. We find substantial grain growth to at least 2 $\mu$m at an early evolutionary stage. Lines of H$_2$O and CO are formed at extremely high temperatures (600-2000 K). The ratio of warm to hot water is the lowest among previous observations of disks with JWST. This and a very strong continuum point toward the relevance of the strong accretion of DG Tau and consequently strong stellar UV irradiation. The pair of jets reveals a rich spectrum of emission lines from ions, in particular producing forbidden lines of [Ne II], [Ne III], [Ar II], [Fe II], and [Ni II]. The forward jet shows a collimated structure as found previously, while the hitherto poorly described, receding jet is more widely dispersed on scales of several arcsec, showing a layered structure with the fastest components being the most collimated. The ionization of the jet gas cannot be reconciled with high-energy radiation from the star itself. Instead, we propose a unified nonequilibrium ionization shock model in which the previously studied X-ray jet plasma continuously cools, recombining ions until, at temperatures around $10^4$ K and below, metals at low ionization stages emit the observed ion lines.

papers.title: Dark Matter Assisted Axion-Magnetic Resonance
papers.abstract: An oscillating axion dark matter (DM) background can enhance the conversion of another relativistic axion into photons when traversing a magnetic field. The DM background rotates photon polarization relative the magnetic orientation, which compensates the photon's and the propagating axion's dispersion relation mismatch. We relate this mechanism to Axion Magnetic Resonance (AMR) and apply it to stellar axions in the starburst galaxy M82. We analyze its enhancement to the resulting X-ray signals while accounting for the finite magnetic domain size, dark matter coherence length, DM density morphology, plasma profiles, and the detector response. We derive strong constraints using existing X-ray data from NuSTAR. We show that this resonant conversion can lead to $\mathcal O(10^2)$ enhancement in the photon-axion conversion probability, improving the upper limits on axion's photon coupling over part of the mass range where ordinary conversion is suppressed. We also show that this type of resonance predicts distinctive features in the hard X-ray spectrum, which is moderately favored by the data over the background only model, yet it is currently still consistent with statistical fluctuations.

papers.title: Multi-Component Axion Dark Matter Revisited and the Role of Ultralight ALPs
papers.abstract: In this work, we revisit the multi-component axion dark matter (DM) scenario and explore the role of ultralight axion-like particles (ALPs). After briefly reviewing maximal axion mixing, we incorporate a stochastic axion mixing mechanism that generalizes it by relaxing the requirement of a uniform hierarchy among the axion decay constants. We find that, depending on the parameters, either the QCD axion or an ALP can dominate the DM abundance after mixing; once axion mass contributions are included, the heaviest ALPs tend to prevail. In a two-component framework, stochastic mixing significantly enlarges the allowed parameter space for the QCD axion decay constant, enabling the QCD axion to constitute the entirety of cold DM. The corresponding ALP mass range remains largely unconstrained by current experiments and is within reach of future searches. In the multi-component case, a larger ALP population leads to the emergence of more ultralight ALPs with large decay constants. These ultralight ALPs represent compelling targets for upcoming axion searches.

papers.title: A Study of Three Intrinsically Luminous Long Period Interacting Eclipsing Binaries in the Galaxy and the Small Magellanic Cloud
papers.abstract: The properties of the eclipsing binaries SMC004701.39-732645.8, SMC005609.41-722809.2 and PW Pup are examined using archival photometric and spectroscopic observations. These systems have orbital periods of hundreds of days, and contain highly evolved components with temperature differences of at least 1000 - 2000K. The SMC systems are among the brightest eclipsing binaries in that galaxy at visible wavelengths, and show excess thermal emission that appears to be typical for luminous K and M giants in that galaxy. A preliminary mass function for SMC004701 suggests a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.8 +/- 0.8 Msolar, whereas the PW Pup mass function indicates a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.2 +/- 0.3 Msolar. Light curve elements are examined for a range of mass ratios using observations at visible and mid-infrared (MIR) wavelengths. The results suggest that SMC004701 may prove to be a double line spectroscopic binary at visible wavelengths. However, with the possible exception of emission from a circumstellar disk, infrared observations will likely be required to detect light from the secondary in the other two systems. All three systems have likely experienced mass transfer, and had components with initial masses that correspond to B spectral types on the main sequence. The light associated with the secondary likely originates from a shell or disk that obscures a hotter central star.

papers.title: DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
papers.abstract: Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins. Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.

papers.title: Hesperos & Eosphoros: A Coupled Differentiable Forced-Photometry Operator and Forward Model for SPHEREx Spectrophotometry
papers.abstract: We present Hesperos & Eosphoros, a forced-photometry operator and a forward model that, respectively, perform and model the spectrophotometric measurement of the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx). Implemented as GPU-accelerated, differentiable JAX programs, the two may be directly composed to measure the response of a downstream product (e.g., the galaxy density field) with respect to a modeled systematic or perturbation through the full measurement pipeline. We describe their design and demonstrate the composition on the response of an astrometric perturbation, and demonstrate how these may be used to generate direct measurement/pipeline response templates $\partial({\rm reconstructed\ density})/\partial({\rm systematic\ amplitude})$ for known image-level effects. Hesperos achieves a factor of $\sim700\times$ increased throughput per node-hour at production scale compared to the prior CPU-based Tractor measurement, previously the limiting step in the experiment's data processing, and propagates automatic derivatives through the full production measurement operator. We validate the measurement operator Hesperos against the public SPHEREx fork of The Tractor, and the forward model Eosphoros against the SPHEREx Sky Simulator and the renders themselves independently against GalSim. Taken together, this represents a powerful increase in capability for scaling, iterating, and optimizing galaxy clustering measurement pipelines.

papers.title: Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordström geometry: new methods at work
papers.abstract: We study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole. In particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-Newtonian expansions. Our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. To solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi method. The perfect agreement of the results highlights the potential of the kink method as a complementary tool for studying wave propagation in black-hole spacetimes.

papers.title: The double copy and perturbative teleparallel gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper we analyze the double copy between gluon and graviton amplitudes within the context of teleparallel gravity. We first set up an effective Lagrangian based on minimal assumptions which reproduces the on-shell amplitudes stemming from the double-copy procedure. By straightforwardly computing the three- and four-point amplitude, this double-copy Lagrangian can be constrained up to a few real parameters when expanding to quartic order. For a specific choice of parameters, we find an exact equivalence with perturbative teleparallel gravity. This suggests that the teleparallel formulation might be well suited to make the double copy more transparent from a Lagrangian viewpoint.

papers.title: Investigating tidal heating in neutron stars via gravitational Raman scattering
papers.abstract: We present a scattering amplitude formalism to study the tidal heating effects of nonspinning neutron stars incorporating both worldline effective field theory and relativistic stellar perturbation theory. In neutron stars, tidal heating arises from fluid viscosity due to various scattering processes in the interior. It also serves as a channel for the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the neutron star and its environment. In the interior of the neutron star, we first derive two master perturbation equations that capture fluid perturbations accurate to linear order in frequency. Remarkably, these equations receive no contribution from bulk viscosity due to a peculiar adiabatic incompressibility which arises in stellar fluid for non-barotropic perturbations. In the exterior, the metric perturbations reduce to the Regge-Wheeler (RW) equation which we solve using the analytical Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi (MST) method. We compute the amplitude for gravitational waves scattering off a neutron star, also known as gravitational Raman scattering. From the amplitude, we obtain expressions for the electric quadrupolar static Love number and the leading dissipation number to all orders in compactness. We then compute the leading dissipation number for various realistic equation-of-state(s) and estimate the change in the number of gravitational wave cycles due to tidal heating during inspiral in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) band. We find that the shear-viscous contribution is small. Even for cold ($T\sim 10^5$K) and weakly compact stars it changes the number of cycles by less than $10^{-2}$, about an order of magnitude below the other conservative 4PN contributions, and it decreases as $T^{-2}$ for hotter stars.

papers.title: Local patch analysis of ACT DR6 convergence map using morphological statistics
papers.abstract: We perform a hierarchical, multi-scale morphological analysis to search for anomalous behavior in the large-scale matter distribution using the Atacama Cosmology Telescope Data Release 6 (ACT DR6) convergence map. Employing Minkowski functionals, contour Minkowski tensors, and Betti numbers, we measure their deviations from ensemble expectations and median values obtained from isotropic $\Lambda$CDM simulations provided by ACT. To assess statistical significance, we develop a general methodology based on the persistence of anomalies across threshold ranges and spatial resolutions, accounting for correlations among the statistics. Analyzing both the full dataset and hemispherical subregions reveals overall consistency with isotropic $\Lambda$CDM expectations. Because localized deviations may be diluted over larger areas, we further examine individual sky patches, identifying several regions with statistically significant deviations that we designate as anomalous. In particular, positive density fluctuations near the CMB Cold Spot are anomalous, exceeding the 99% confidence level, and overlap with a previously reported anomalous southern spot in Planck CMB temperature data. Analysis of the corresponding null map indicates potential contamination from residual foregrounds or instrumental systematics. Comparing the anomalous patches in ACT with those from a previous Planck convergence map analysis reveals no overlapping regions, suggesting that the Planck anomalies are likely attributable to noise. Further investigation of these atypical patches, considering residual foregrounds, instrumental systematics, reconstruction noise, and independent large-scale structure surveys, is warranted to determine their physical origin.

papers.title: The Stellar Populations and Rest-Frame Colors of Star-Forming Galaxies at $z \approx 8$: Exploring the Impact of Filter Choice and Star Formation History Assumption with JADES
papers.abstract: Our understanding of the physical properties of star-forming galaxies during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR, at $z > 6$) suffers from degeneracies among the apparent properties of the stars, the nebular gas, and the dust. These degeneracies are most prominent with photometry, which has insufficient (1) spectral resolution and (2) rest-frame spectral coverage. We explore ways to break these degeneracies with a sample of $N = 22$ high-redshift star-forming galaxies at $7 < z_{\mathrm{phot}} \leq 9$, using some of the deepest existing imaging from JWST/NIRCam and JWST/MIRI with JADES. Key to this study is the imaging from JWST/MIRI at $7.7\ \mu\mathrm{m}$, which provides coverage of the rest-frame $I$-band at the observed redshifts. We infer stellar population properties and rest-frame colors using a variety of filter sets and star formation history assumptions to explore the impact of these choices. Evaluating these quantities both with and without the $7.7\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ data point shows that dense spectral coverage with JWST/NIRCam (eight or more filters, including at least one medium-band) can compensate for lacking the rest-frame $I$-band coverage for the vast majority ($\approx 80\%$) of our sample. Furthermore, these galaxy properties are most consistently determined by assuming the delayed-tau star formation history, which provides the smallest offsets and scatters around these offsets when including JWST/MIRI. Within extragalactic surveys like JADES and CEERS, our findings suggest that robust characterization of the stellar population properties and rest-frame colors for high-redshift star-forming galaxies is possible with JWST/NIRCam alone at $z \approx 8$.

papers.title: To collapse or not to collapse: Halo evolution with self-interacting dark matter mass segregation
papers.abstract: Surprisingly compact substructures in galaxies and galaxy clusters, but also field halos, have been observed by gravitational lensing. They could be difficult to explain with collisionless dark matter (DM). To explain those objects, recent studies focused on the gravothermal collapse that halos consisting of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) can undergo. However, simple models of elastic scattering could face problems explaining those compact objects during very later stages of the collapse and the post-collapse phase, where a black hole may have formed from DM. We aim to explain compact halos while avoiding the gravothermal catastrophe to which typical SIDM models are subject. Therefore, we investigate the evolution of a DM halo for an SIDM model consisting of two species with unequal masses, which features only interactions between the different species but not within themselves. Employing $N$-body simulations, we study the effect of unequal-mass SIDM models on the evolution of an isolated DM halo. In particular, the late stages of its evolution with high central densities are simulated. We find that our two-species SIDM models can produce density cores with their size depending on the mass ratio of the two species. Moreover, mass segregation caused by the unequal particle masses leads to a finite final density state or at least a slowly growing density, which depends on the mass ratio and the mass fraction of the two DM species. SIDM models consisting of two DM species can simultaneously explain DM halos with density cores, as well as systems that are denser in their centre than expected from collisionless DM, while avoiding the gravothermal catastrophe. They are a compelling alternative to single-species models, offering a rich phenomenology.

papers.title: Influence of perfect fluid dark matter on shadow observables of Yang-Mills modified charged black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) on Yang--Mills--inspired charged black holes, with a particular focus on the resulting modifications to key black hole observables. By embedding a PFDM term into the spacetime geometry, we examine the alterations in shadow morphology, photon geodesics, and the associated energy emission spectra. Our analysis reveals that PFDM induces notable deviations in the shadow size, shape, and circularity, and significantly impacts the stability of circular orbits. Furthermore, the energy emission rate exhibits a strong dependence on both the Yang--Mills charge and the dark matter distribution. These results indicate that environmental effects arising from dark matter can imprint observable signatures on black hole shadows and radiation processes, offering a potential pathway to constrain dark matter models and probe non-Kerr geometries with forthcoming high-precision observations such as those from the Event Horizon Telescope and next-generation interferometers.
papers.comments: 28 Pages, 37 Figures, published in The European Physical Journal C. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Prospect on constraining environment-dependent dilaton model from gravitational redshift measurements
papers.abstract: Scalar-tensor gravity represents a natural extension of general relativity. This paper investigates the prospects for constraining the environmentally dependent dilaton through atomic-clock comparisons across media of different densities. Using the scalar Compton wavelength, we assess how the finite size of the surrounding medium and screening by the clock enclosure limit the accessible region. To test the continuous-density approximation for dilute media, we model matter as a periodic lattice of spherical particles and compare an analytic Neumann solution with a three-dimensional finite-element solution on the cubic box. The continuous and discrete models give indistinguishable redshift predictions near the $10^{-20}$ and $10^{-25}$ benchmarks. In the strong-coupling regime, differences become apparent on redshift contours of order $10^{-46}$ or lower. Under the assumed environmental and instrumental conditions, comparisons involving a dense medium identify a window for probing smaller values of $A_2$, offering a gravitational-redshift test complementary to existing fifth-force searches.

papers.title: Ionizing Photon Production Efficiencies and Chemical Abundances at Cosmic Dawn Revealed by Ultra-Deep Rest-Frame Optical Spectroscopy of JADES-GS-z14-0
papers.abstract: JWST has discovered an early period of galaxy formation that was more vigorous than expected, which has challenged our understanding of the early Universe. In this work, we present the longest spectroscopic integration ever acquired by JWST/MIRI ($t_{\mathrm{obs}} \approx 51\ \mathrm{hr}$). This spectrum covers the brightest rest-frame optical nebular emission lines for the luminous galaxy JADES-GS-z14-0 at $z = 14.18$. Most notably, we detect $[\mathrm{OIII}] \lambda\lambda 4959,5007$ at $\approx 14 \sigma$ and $\mathrm{H}\alpha$ at $\approx 4 \sigma$ with these ultra-deep observations. These lines reveal that JADES-GS-z14-0 has low dust attenuation with a recent star-formation rate of $\mathrm{SFR} \approx 8 \pm 2\ M_{\odot} / \mathrm{yr}$, star-formation rate surface density of $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SFR}} \approx 20 \pm 5\ M_{\odot}/\mathrm{yr}/\mathrm{kpc}^{2}$, and ionizing photon production efficiency of $\xi_{\mathrm{ion}} \approx 10^{25.3 \pm 0.1}\ \mathrm{Hz/erg}$. Using standard strong-line diagnostics, we infer a gas-phase oxygen abundance of $[\mathrm{O/H}] \approx -1.2 \pm 0.2$ ($\approx 6\%\ Z_{\odot}$), carbon-to-oxygen ratio of $[\mathrm{C/O}] \approx -0.4 \pm 0.2$, ionization parameter of $\mathrm{log}_{10}(U) \gtrsim -2.4$, and density of $n_{\mathrm{H}} \approx 690 \pm 200\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$. Using detailed photoionization modeling, we instead derive $[\mathrm{O/H}] \approx -0.2_{-0.4}^{+0.4}$ ($\approx 60\%\ Z_{\odot}$). The inferred properties of JADES-GS-z14-0 are similar to those measured for similarly luminous galaxies at $z > 10$ with previous MIRI/Spectroscopy, such as GHZ2/GLASSz12, GN-z11, and MACS0647-JD1. Existing simulations are unable to reproduce the empirical and inferred properties of JADES-GS-z14-0. This work demonstrates an important step toward understanding the formation of the first stars and heavy elements in the Universe. [Abridged]

papers.title: Exact general solutions for cosmological scalar field evolution in a vacuum-energy dominated expansion
papers.abstract: We derive exact general solutions (as opposed to attractor particular solutions) for the evolution of a scalar field $\phi$ in a universe dominated by a background fluid with equation of state parameter $w_B = -1$, extending earlier work on exact solutions with $w_B > -1$. Straightfoward exact solutions exist when the evolution is described by a linear differential equation, corresponding to constant, linear, and quadratic potentials. In the nonlinear case, exact solutions are derived for $V = V_0\ln \phi$, $V = V_0 \phi^{1/2}$ and $V = V_0/\phi$, and the logarithmic potential also yields an exact first integral. These complicated parametric solutions are considerably less useful than those derived previously for a universe dominated by a barotropic fluid such as matter or radiation with $w_B > -1$. However, we generalize the slow-roll approximation and show that it applies to all sufficiently flat potentials in the case of a vacuum-dominated expansion, while it never applies when the universe is dominated by a background fluid with $w_B > -1$.

papers.title: Spiral Density Waves and Torque Balance in the Kerr Geometry
papers.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in relativistic accretion discs are a key science target for the upcoming LISA mission. Existing models of disc-EMRI interactions typically rely on crude dynamical friction or Newtonian planetary migration prescriptions, which fail to capture the relativistic fluid response induced by the binary potential. In this work we address this gap by providing the relativistic calculation. We apply standard methods from self-force theory, black hole perturbation theory, and relativistic stellar perturbation theory to compute the relativistic analogue of the spiral density wave and torque-balance results underlying planetary migration. Specifically, we calculate the response of a perfect fluid disc to the perturbing potential of an EMRI, consistently incorporating pressure effects. Using a master enthalpy-like variable and linearised fluid theory, we present a set of proof-of-principle calculations that reconstruct the fluid perturbations and relativistic spiral arm structure for a range of spin values in the Kerr geometry. We derive a relativistic torque-balance equation that enables us to compute and compare local torques with the angular momentum advected through the disc, finding striking agreement when applied to our relativistic disc-EMRI solutions. This opens a promising route towards establishing torque-balance relations between integrated disc torques arising from fluid perturbations and the forces acting on EMRIs embedded in matter.

papers.title: Approximate Decoherence, Recoherence and Records in Isolated Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Using the framework of decoherent histories, we study which past events leave detectable records in isolated quantum systems under the realistic assumption that decoherence is approximate and not perfect. Using tools from quantum state discrimination, we establish asymptotically for a large class of (pseudo-)random histories how the strength of decoherence changes the number of reliable records, i.e., we quantitatively answer the question: when can approximate decoherence be approximated by exact decoherence? In addition, we reveal a clear decoherence structure for long histories based on a numerically exact solution of a random matrix model that, as we argue, captures generic aspects of decoherence. In particular, we observe strong recoherences for maverick histories that are statistical outliers with respect to Born's rule. From the perspective of the Many Worlds Interpretation, our results reveal a "branch selection problem" and shed light on the emergence of Born's rule and the theory confirmation problem.

papers.title: Statistics of time and frequency-averaged spectra in gravitational-wave background searches
papers.abstract: Time series analysis from gravitational-wave detectors often relies on the assumption that time chunks, or frequency bins, are uncorrelated. We discuss the validity of this approximation in the context of searches for stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds. We examine the impact of averaging over time and frequency, a reduction technique commonly employed to minimize the computational expense of likelihood evaluations. We introduce an analytical tool based on Fisher information to quantify the error in parameter inference arising from ignoring these effects. Finally, we address the issue of locally stationary processes and optimal time chunking. As an application, we study examples based on simulated data of the LISA space mission.

papers.title: Out of oxygen: Extremely metal-poor galaxy candidates identified at $2.5 < z < 6.5$ with deep JADES medium-band imaging
papers.abstract: JWST is beginning to uncover a population of extremely metal-poor galaxies (EMPGs, $Z < 1\%~\mathrm{Z}_\odot$) at $z > 3$, mostly through serendipitous NIRSpec discoveries and blind slitless spectroscopy. To accelerate our understanding of pristine star formation, we further develop a methodology to identify EMPG candidates from photometry, using the extensive deep medium-band imaging from JADES. Our EMPG candidates at $2.5 < z < 6.5$ exhibit strong photometric boosts by H$\alpha$, yet correspondingly weak boosts by [O III] + H$\beta$, likely indicating extremely low metallicity to explain their lack of [O III] emission. We further demand our EMPG candidates to have strong Balmer jumps, as revealed by medium-band imaging, to ensure that they are young starbursts, as opposed to broad-line AGN/LRDs, though contamination by dusty/dense-gas starbursts and highly-obscured AGN remains a concern. SED-fitting with near-pristine models (${\sim}0.1$-$1\%~\mathrm{Z}_\odot$) indicates that our 14 EMPG candidates are low-mass (median $M_* \approx 10^{6.7}~\mathrm{M}_\odot$), faint dwarf galaxies ($M_\mathrm{UV} \approx -16.9$), with high ionizing photon production efficiencies ($\log\, (\xi_\mathrm{ion, obs}/\mathrm{(Hz\ erg^{-1})}) \approx 26.0$). Hence these are plausible sites of near-pristine star formation, comprising ${\sim}0.02$-$0.4\%$ of $2.5 < z < 6.5$ galaxies at $-19 < M_\mathrm{UV} < -16$. We discuss this extremely metal-poor extension to the mass-metallicity relation. We forecast that deep (${\sim}28$ h) NIRCam slitless spectroscopy can identify bright EMPGs through strong H$\beta$ but lack of [O III] emission, or secure the redshifts of fainter systems through H$\alpha$ detections. Highly-multiplexed NIRSpec spectroscopy offers an alternate route to discovering the faintest pristine galaxies out to $z=10$, without requiring deep medium-band/MIRI imaging to identify secure candidates.

papers.title: Memory effect for generalized modes in pp-wave spacetimes
papers.abstract: The memory effect of test particles interacting with pp-wave Gaussian pulses is investigated for { higher-order polynomial pp--wave modes beyond the standard quadrupolar $+$ and $\times$ profiles}. Massive geodesic equations are solved numerically for several values of the { polynomial index $m$}, allowing the analysis of velocity and energy memory effects. In order to eliminate possible coordinate artifacts, the study is formulated in terms of the relative motion between two test particles. The results show that the relative kinetic energy variation exhibits a quartic dependence on the wave amplitude in the regime of low initial velocities. The coefficient of this scaling is found to depend on the { transverse polynomial structure of the wave, reflecting the spatial gradients associated with the different modes}. It is further shown that the energy memory effect is determined by the integrated tidal field, linking the permanent change in the relative kinetic energy to the history of the spacetime curvature carried by the wave.

papers.title: Convergence of the post-Newtonian series in the quasicircular, nonprecessing, and comparable-mass regime
papers.abstract: Post-Newtonian (PN) theory provides the analytic foundation for modeling the early inspiral of binary black holes. However, as an asymptotic series, successive PN orders do not necessarily improve agreement with the full nonlinear dynamics. While this has been explored in the extreme-mass-ratio (EMR) limit, comparable-mass systems most relevant to current observations have not been benchmarked as systematically at high PN order. We study the convergence of the PN series for non-spinning and quasi-circular systems by comparing the PN energy flux at future null infinity to a long, high-accuracy numerical relativity (NR) simulation. To enable a gauge-consistent comparison, we place both descriptions in the same BMS frame and calibrate the intrinsic PN parameters by fitting to the NR waveform in the early inspiral. We find that for orbital velocities $v\lesssim0.45$, higher PN orders continue to reduce the PN--NR flux discrepancy, with EMR terms beyond 4.5PN providing further improvement in the late inspiral. The improvement with PN order is non-monotonic with local extrema around 2.5PN and 4PN. Thus, for the comparable-mass flux comparison considered here, the first local minimum of the finite-order residual does not identify the best PN truncation order among the orders available. As $v$ approaches $\sim 0.5$ near the innermost circular orbit, higher PN orders no longer improve the agreement between NR and PN, indicating a loss of convergence. These results motivate continued high-order PN calculations and clarify the NR accuracy needed to validate them.

papers.title: Another Look at the Weak-Field Limit of Generalized Hybrid Metric-Palatini Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the weak-field regime of generalized hybrid metric-Palatini theories, described by a generic function $f(R,\mathcal{R})$, where $R$ is the metric Ricci scalar and $\mathcal{R}$ is constructed from an independent torsionless connection. Linearizing the field equations about Minkowski spacetime, we show, without using the scalar-tensor representation, that the theory propagates the usual massless spin-2 mode and two massive scalar modes, with an effective gravitational coupling. The absence of tachyonic and ghostlike instabilities at the linearized level, together with the nondegeneracy of the scalar sector, is shown to impose algebraic restrictions on the derivatives of $f(R,\mathcal{R})$ evaluated on the Minkowski background, which generalize previously obtained conditions. The Newtonian limit for an extended static source is derived, yielding a gravitational potential with two Yukawa corrections whose amplitudes are fixed by the scalar residues, while finite-size effects are encoded in source-dependent form factors. We determine the conditions under which the usual Newtonian limit is recovered and derive the effective post-Newtonian parameter $\gamma_\Sigma$ governing light propagation. Finally, we compute the radial epicyclic frequency and the corresponding anomalous periapsis advance, and compare it with planetary precession data to constrain the parameters of a viable hierarchical scalar-mass regime.
